tagline: Out of Monument Valley, over the San Juan, on to Bluff.
intro: US 163 comes up out of Arizona straight into Monument Valley, a Navajo tribal park, past the turn for the visitor center and on among the red rock spires that so many western movies have used. It runs northeast to Mexican Hat, crosses the San Juan River and leaves the Navajo Nation, then heads east over Comb Ridge to Bluff.
The road began in 1910 as State Route 47 and took its present number in 1970, when the federal highways of the Four Corners were rearranged.

moments.title: Forrest Gump hill
moments.text: Near Utah mile marker 13 a view area has picked up the movie's name, and fans of the film come to re-create the scene where its hero ends his cross-country run.

moments.title: Mexican Hat
moments.text: A town of 21 at the 2020 census, named for a sombrero-shaped rock on its northeast edge, where the byway crosses the San Juan River on a historic bridge.

moments.title: Bluff
moments.text: About 230 Mormon settlers arrived here in April 1880 after forging some 200 miles of their own trail, down through the Hole in the Rock, and named the town for the bluffs.
